insights.claim: The odh-notebook-controller mutating webhook injects a kube-rbac-proxy sidecar into every notebook pod, making per-notebook authentication a hard dependency on the kube-rbac-proxy container image.
insights.reasoning: The kube-rbac-proxy-image flag is required at startup (the controller exits if unset). The mutating webhook injects this container as a sidecar named 'kube-rbac-proxy' into every notebook pod. This creates a hard runtime dependency: if the image is unavailable or misconfigured, notebook pods cannot start with authentication.

insights.claim: The controller adaptively configures TLS cipher suites from the OpenShift APIServer TLS profile, falling back to hardened defaults on non-OpenShift clusters or transient API errors.
insights.reasoning: At startup the controller attempts to fetch config.openshift.io/v1/APIServer to read the TLS profile. It distinguishes transient API errors (where it registers a watcher for self-healing) from permanent absence (non-OpenShift cluster). This adaptive pattern ensures the controller can run on both OpenShift and vanilla Kubernetes while preferring platform-managed TLS posture.

insights.claim: The DataSciencePipelinesApplication CRD integration is gracefully optional: the controller skips Elyra secret provisioning when the DSPA CRD is not installed or no DSPA instance exists.
insights.reasoning: The getDSPAInstance function explicitly handles both IsNotFound (no DSPA CR in namespace) and IsNoMatchError (CRD not installed) by returning nil without error. This makes the DSPA integration a soft dependency that does not block notebook creation when the pipelines component is absent.
